title: Starter ShellKit: 15-minute Playloop and Troubleshoot Notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, opinionated playbook for getting an engineer from zero to an instrumented sample call using ShellKit (a tiny CLI wrapper we hand out in workshops). Goal: 15 minutes of hands-on success, plus a short set of troubleshoot heuristics so the first failure doesn't become a support ticket.

Audience:
- Fast-moving product engineers who want to integrate Redwood in a PoC/app prototype.
- Solutions engineers running 30–60 min demos.
- Internal advocates and hackathon leads.

Scope and constraints:
- Minimal prerequisites: bash/zsh, curl, node 18+, API key.
- Focused on hosted API flows (text generation + streaming) and basic telemetry.
- Not a deep dive on dedicated/private deployment — refer to Private-Deploy playbooks for that.

Quick checklist (pre-demo, 5 min):
- [ ] Create API key in Console (team/demo-key).
- [ ] Install the shellkit: curl -fsSL install.redwood.dev/shellkit | sh
- [ ] Confirm network egress to api.redwood.ai: curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health
- [ ] Clone sample repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter && cd sdk-starter/shellkit

15-minute playloop (timed steps):
- Minute 0–2: Introduce files in the repo (README, .env.example, simple.sh, stream.sh).
- Minute 2–5: Copy .env.example -> .env, paste API key. Tip: use a temporary key with 1h TTL for demos.
- Minute 5–8: Run basic sync generation:
  ./simple.sh "Write a one-sentence summary of Redwood Inference"
  Expected: a single JSON response line with text and token_count.
- Minute 8–12: Run streaming example to show partial output and latency feel:
  ./stream.sh "Explain batching in one paragraph"
  Observe: incremental chunks, no long delay.
- Minute 12–15: Inspect telemetry output (local shellkit prints):
  cat .redwood/telemetry.log | tail -n 20
  Look for: request_id, latency_ms, model:variant, tokens_in/out.

Minimal example snippets to paste during demos:
- simple.sh (bash):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  source .env
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"gptx-mini","input":"'$1'","max_tokens":120}' | jq -r '.output[0].text'

- stream.sh (bash using SSE-ish helper):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  source .env
  ./shellkit stream --model gptx-mini --prompt "$1" --on-chunk 'printf "%s" "$CHUNK"'

Common failure modes (fast triage):
- 401 Unauthorized:
  - Cause: API key missing or pasted with whitespace.
  - Quick fix: echo "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | wc -c (should be > 0). Recreate console key if needed.
- 502 / timeout from api.redwood.ai:
  - Cause: transient edge or blocked outbound port (corporate firewall).
  - Quick fix: curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health; if DNS fails, try nslookup api.redwood.ai.
- Streaming shows nothing (hangs):
  - Cause: proxy, chunked responses not allowed by network.
  - Quick fix: run non-stream example. Note it down in the ticket.
- Very high latency (>1s per token):
  - Cause: chosen model/region mismatch, or local rate limiting.
  - Quick fix: switch to gptx-mini or route to hosted-fast region via --region flag.

Telem + instrumentation checklist (ops-friendly):
- Ensure shellkit writes per-request JSON lines to .redwood/telemetry.log with these fields: request_id, utc_ts, model, region, latency_ms, token_in, token_out, error_code.
- Add an optional env var REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEM for privacy demos to turn off telemetry.
- Advisory: never send customer PII in telemetry; redwood console automatically redacts top-level text in sandbox mode but demoers should still avoid real PII.

Onboarding heuristics for Solutions Engineers (notes):
- Start the customer on sandbox key, show quick wins with a summarization example, then switch to their dataset prompt.
- Bring the console usage dashboard up while demoing to show real-time token/billing visibility — this is a strong trust signal.
- Prep a fallback prompt in case the model hallucinates (a short instruction like: "If you are unsure, say 'I don't know' and ask for clarifying context").

Mini runbook for escalating a stuck demo:
- Step 1: Collect .redwood/telemetry.log and the exact prompt used.
- Step 2: Reproduce locally with a newly minted temp key (to rule out key scope).
- Step 3: If still failing, raise a support ticket with tags: demo, SE, urgent and attach logs + time window + region.

Follow-ups and improvements (Riley action items):
- Add a tiny interactive step in stream.sh to demonstrate function/tool calling soon (prototype exists in GH link).
- Build a 1-click CloudShell snippet that sets env + runs simple.sh to remove copy/paste friction.
- Workshop metric: >80% of attendees should successfully run simple.sh inside 15 minutes. We'll run an A/B test with/without CloudShell to measure.

Open questions for review: (inconclusive items to decide)
- Do we ship a signed demo key with 1-hour TTL for all internal SEs or keep SEs creating keys per demo?
- Should telemetry default to on for internal demos, or opt-in? Security team preference was opt-out for public demos.

References and quick links:
- Sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter/tree/main/shellkit
- GH prototype for interactive stream helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-helper/pull/14
- Related internal RFC: confluence:DEVEXP/ShellKit-Onramp-2025

Appendix: quick checklist for packaging into a workshop slide (30s):
1) Slide 1: Why ShellKit exists (remove friction + show telemetry).
2) Slide 2: 3-step starter (install, set key, run simple.sh).
3) Slide 3: Troubleshoot cheat sheet (copy 3 bulleted fixes).
4) Slide 4: Next steps (embed in CloudShell, automate key rotate, link to PR).

End of notes.

Small-print: this is a working doc; please add comments inline or file PRs against the sample repo. If you're an SE and want a signed demo key, DM Riley on Slack.
